Subject: fix(public): group player cards by team and order them by batting position
CommitMessage:
fix(public): group player cards by team and order them by batting position

Addresses the fourth and last finding on issue #475. P01-F09 and P02-F06 recorded
that the player cards on a fixture page interleave both sides in no discernible
order. P01, who reads scorecards fluently, called them "a pile of cards"; P02,
with no cricket background, could not see one team's players together. Both said

Author: Ben Swartz
Subject: feat(submissions): let the guided CSV express a dismissal
CommitMessage:
feat(submissions): let the guided CSV express a dismissal

Issue #536. The season upload package contract already accepted wickets, and the
JSON upload path carried them end to end, but csvCandidates built each event from
a fixed column set that had no dismissal fields. Every delivery submitted through
the guided CSV therefore normalised to an empty wickets array, and a submitter
using the shipped template could not record a wicket at all.

Adds twelve columns to the CSV template: wicketKind, the dismissed player as a
source identifier and name pair, and three fielder slots each carrying a source
identifier, a name and a substitute flag. csvCandidates maps them into the
existing seasonUploadWicketSchema shape. The dismissed player and each fielder are
built with the same helper as the striker and bowler, so they resolve by name
through the reference resolver under the rules established in #360.

A blank wicketKind with any other dismissal column filled is reported as
CSV_WICKET_KIND_MISSING rather than dropped, so a submitter who omits the kind is
told rather than silently losing the wicket.

The JSON template gains a second example event carrying a caught dismissal, since
the format already supported wickets but the shipped template never demonstrated
one.

The column limits were chosen from the corpus rather than assumed. Of 174,342
deliveries carrying a wicket, 10 carry more than one, and the contract already
caps an event at two. Of 116,622 wickets naming a fielder, 5,872 name more than
one and the maximum anywhere is three, every one of them a run out. The CSV
therefore carries one dismissal per delivery and up to three fielders; anything
beyond that must use the JSON package, and both limits are documented.

No change is made to packages/contracts, the OpenAPI document, the database or any
validation rule. The relationship between dismissal kind and fielders continues to
be enforced in one place, by submissionWicketSchema.

Refs #536

Subject: fix(public): show the non-boundary flag only where it is meaningful
CommitMessage:
fix(public): show the non-boundary flag only where it is meaningful

Addresses the third finding on issue #475. P01-F12 and P02-F22 recorded that
every delivery in a calculation trace displayed "Non-boundary: No", which one
participant read as a double negative of unclear purpose and the other saw only
as a column of identical values.

The trace now shows a Boundary row only on deliveries whose runs were run rather
than hit to the boundary, and shows nothing on the rest. Frontend coverage
asserts both halves: the row is absent where the flag is false and present where
it is true.

The field is not removed from the event exports. Both export endpoints are
public and unversioned under /api/v1, runs.nonBoundary is required by
packages/contracts and by openapi.yaml under additionalProperties: false, and
docs/api/versioning.md classifies removing a field as breaking and requires a
deprecation marking, migration guidance, a retirement date and a migration
period. The export half of this finding therefore cannot be completed within
Sprint 2 and the acceptance criterion is corrected on the issue.

The derivation, database and API responses are unchanged. This is presentation
only.

Subject: fix(public): add an API entry to the footer and cover the download confirmation
CommitMessage:
fix(public): add an API entry to the footer and cover the download confirmation

Addresses two of the four findings on issue #475, both raised by external
participants during Sprint 2 public and analyst user testing.

P01-F27: there was no API or Developers entry in the navigation or the footer,
and the only route to API information was through the site logo. The public
footer now carries an API entry linking to the API section of the home page,
which is given an anchor and scrolled to on navigation, since client-side
routing does not scroll to a fragment on its own.

P01-F24 and P02-F18: no on-screen confirmation was given that a download had
occurred. The confirmation is present on main and was not present in the build
under test. No production change was required. A frontend test now covers it,
asserting on the export section's own status region so that text elsewhere on
the page cannot satisfy it, and requiring the region to be empty before the
download and silent while the export is still preparing.

Both participants were confirmed to have used the control now at
EventExportControls.tsx, matched by the export panel wording recorded in the
session files against the source of commit 249f9be227. It is the only event
export control in the application.

Out of scope: the player card ordering and the runsNonBoundary flag, which are
the remaining two items on #475.
